Commentary.Commentary: Done with this game - That wraps up this game. Nepal have walked away with the bragging rights against fellow Associate side UAE after a well-rounded performance. The action continues as teams move through their warm-up fixtures, fine-tuning plans and ironing out a few creases. Wednesday, 4th February 2026, offers a packed schedule with Scotland facing Namibia, Afghanistan meeting West Indies, Pakistan up against Ireland, and a blockbuster to close the day as India take on South Africa. We hope you will join us again. Until then, goodbye and cheers.

Flash, fall, fix - With the bat, UAE produced an effort that brought smiles and a mild headache in equal measure. The Powerplay was productive and promising, but the innings lost its way soon after. The scoring rate stalled, and wickets fell with stubborn regularity, one feeding the other. At 5 down for 66, Harshit Kaushik and Sohaib Khan stepped in with a timely rescue act. Their 68-run partnership gave the innings much-needed oxygen and brought the total close to 150, but it ultimately was not enough.

Flavourless bowling from UAE - This game laid bare plenty of problems for the UAE. There was a flicker of early spark, driven almost entirely by three excellent overs from Muhammad Rohid, who bowled with genuine fire and venom. Beyond that, the bowling lacked bite and purpose. The spinners found little from the surface and did themselves no favours with inconsistent lines. The end result was a defeat that will sting and demand some hard reflection.

A statement win by Nepal! What a commanding performance! Chasing a target of 146, Nepal wobbled early at 45 for 3, but that was as shaky as it got. Dipendra Singh Airee (50* off 31 balls) and Aarif Sheikh (61* off 37 balls) then took complete control with an unbeaten 103-run stand that oozed composure and intent. They blended caution with timely aggression, shut the door firmly on any UAE comeback and cruised home with plenty of overs to spare. A chase paced to perfection and finished in style.

FOUR! That seals it, and in style. Short on middle, Sheikh turns inside the crease and clouts it behind square leg for the winning boundary. The hundred-run partnership comes up as well, and Nepal cruise home with three overs to spare, a comprehensive seven-wicket win.
